claim: The Bock Casemates are part of a 23 km underground tunnel system carved into the rock and received the Tripadvisor 2026 Travellers' Choice Award; address is Montée de Clausen, L-1343 Luxembourg.
quote: system of underground galleries and tunnels stretching over 23 km ... received Tripadvisor's 2026 Travellers' Choice Award ... Montée de Clausen, 1343 Luxembourg

claim: Bock Casemates open March 1 to November 2, 2026, 10:00-17:00 (to 18:00 in summer); adult ticket €8, Kulturpass €1.50.
quote: open from March 1 to November 2, 2026, with hours from 10:00-17:00, extending to 18:00 during summer months ... Adult tickets cost 8 EUR ... Kulturpass rate of €1.50

claim: Mudam (Park Dräi Eechelen, Kirchberg) opens Tue-Sun 10:00-18:00, Wed to 21:00 with free entry Wed 18:00-21:00; full price €10, reduced €7, free under 21 and for students.
quote: Tuesday–Sunday: 10:00–18:00 ... Wednesday: 10:00–21:00 ... Full price: €10 ... Reduced rate: €7 ... Free: Children under 21, students ... Wednesday 18:00 – 21:00

claim: Since 29 February 2020 all public transport in Luxembourg (trains, trams, RGTR/TICE/AVL buses) has been free for residents and tourists; only 1st-class rail still requires a ticket.
quote: Since 29 February 2020, public transport has been free for everybody, residents as well as tourists ... trains, trams and buses (RGTR, TICE, AVL). However, the only exception are tickets and subscriptions for the 1st class

claim: LuxembourgPass (formerly LuxembourgCard) gives free access to 80+ tourist sites; individual cards cost €14/1 day, €22/2 days, €31/3 days, family/group up to 5 €31/€54/€77.
quote: free access or access at reduced prices to more than 80 tourist sites ... €14 for one day, €22 for two days, and €31 for three days ... groups and families of up to five people, the cost is €31, €54, and €77

claim: Grand Ducal Palace summer tours run 18 July to 30 August 2026, in Luxembourgish/French/English/German; adults €18, children 4-12 €9, under 4 free; book via LCTO.
quote: from Saturday 18 July to Sunday 30 August 2026 ... Adults: €18.00 ... Children (4-12 years): €9.00 ... Luxemburgish, French, English, and German

claim: The Chemin de la Corniche, dubbed 'the most beautiful balcony of Europe' by Batty Weber, runs along 17th-century Spanish/French ramparts from the Bock promontory to the Holy Ghost Citadel overlooking the Alzette valley and Grund.
quote: the most beautiful balcony of Europe ... along the Alzette valley on the ramparts built by the Spaniards and the French in the 17th century, from the Bock Promontory up to the lower part of the Holy Ghost Citadel

claim: Philharmonie Luxembourg's 2026/27 season features Sir Simon Rattle with Bach at its centre, plus the atlântico festival and a John Coltrane centenary tribute.
quote: 2026/27 season featuring performances ranging from Sir Simon Rattle to Luxembourg's Duo Vershinina-Lee, with Bach taking center stage ... tributes to John Coltrane's 100th birthday

claim: MNHA/Nationalmusée um Fëschmaart's permanent collections are free; combined ticket with Musée Dräi Eechelen (Kirchberg) is €12 on the same day.
quote: The permanent exhibitions are free of charge ... admission to both museums (Musée Dräi Eechelen & Nationalmusée um Fëschmaart), valid on the same day: €12

claim: Notre-Dame Cathedral is open daily except during services with free admission; its crypt added 1935-37 holds the tomb of John the Blind and Grand Ducal family members.
quote: open daily, except during services, and admission is free ... crypt was added between 1935 and 1937 ... resting place of John the Blind, King of Bohemia and Count of Luxembourg, as well as deceased members of the Grand Ducal family

claim: Neumünster Abbey in the Grund, built in 1688 on the former Benedictine Altmünster site, is now a cultural centre hosting the European Institute of Cultural Routes plus concerts and exhibitions; the Saint-Esprit/Grund lift connects upper and lower town daily until 02:00 (04:00 Fri/Sat).
quote: Neumünster Abbey was built in 1688 ... home of the European Institute of Cultural Routes ... Grund elevator that connects Plateau du Saint-Esprit ... Sunday to Thursday from 6.30 am to 2 am and Fridays and Saturdays from 6.30 am to 4 am

claim: The Pétrusse Casemates have reopened after security works with new scenography and light installations; access 7 days a week every 15 min from 09:45 to 17:00 (last admission), entry at Place de la Constitution.
quote: After extensive enhancement and security works, the Pétrusse Casemates reopened with a cutting-edge scenography and mesmerising light installations ... 7 days a week, every 15 minutes, from 09:45 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

claim: Moutfort lies about 13 km from Luxembourg City centre, roughly a 12-minute drive, and is reachable by RGTR bus line 411.
quote: Moutfort to Luxembourg - 3 ways to travel via line 411 bus ... driving distance between Moutfort and Luxembourg is 8 miles, and it takes approximately 12 minutes

claim: Caves Bernard-Massard in Grevenmacher offers ~1-hour guided cellar tours with audiovisual presentation and tasting, Wednesday to Sunday, April to end of October, from €8 (1 glass) for adults and €5 for children 3-15, bookable online.
quote: Availability: from Wednesday to Sunday, April to the end of October. ... Individual visit with tasting (1 glass): €8.00 per person. Children ages 3-15: €5.00.

claim: MS Princesse Marie-Astrid Moselle cruises cost €24 per adult, with under-6 free, under-12 half-price, and bicycles transported free of charge subject to capacity.
quote: Price per adult: 24 euros incl. VAT ... Under 6 years: complimentary ... Under 12 years: 50% reduction ... Bicycles: transported at no charge (subject to capacity)

claim: The MS Princesse Marie-Astrid runs a fixed Easter-to-September timetable from its Grevenmacher base, calling at Wasserbillig, Wormeldange, Stadtbredimus, Remich, Bech-Kleinmacher and Schengen as well as Trier.
quote: There are several stops between Trier (Germany), Wasserbillig, Grevenmacher, Wormeldange, Stadtbredimus, Remich, Bech-Kleinmacher and Schengen.

claim: Remich's quay is the home port of Navitours, which operates the River Diva, Roude Léiw and Muselschëff for shorter Moselle excursions alongside the Marie-Astrid.
quote: Navitours ... Vessels: River Diva (82 meters), Roude Léiw, and Muselschëff ... Address: Quai de la Moselle, L-5553 Remich

claim: Caves St Martin in Remich runs 75-90 minute guided tours through nearly a kilometre of limestone tunnels at a constant 12°C, with a Discovery tasting of one Crémant plus two Grand Premier Cru wines for roughly €12-15, by reservation 48 hours ahead.
quote: Guided tours including tasting cost around €12–15 ... walk through underground tunnels—nearly a kilometre long—carved into solid limestone rock ... temperature in the tunnels is a constant, damp 12°C ... Reservations have to be made 48 hours in advance.

claim: Domaine Mathis Bastian, a five-generation family estate on the Primerberg/Wellenstein slopes above Remich, accepts cellar visits and tastings by appointment from April to September.
quote: Visits of the vineyard and the cellar can be reserved from April to September. Visits and tastings can be organized on appointment.

claim: Domaine Alice Hartmann in Wormeldange (rue Principale 72-74) is open for visits by appointment, typically Friday afternoons, and is renowned for its Wormeldange Koeppchen Riesling and Crémant served at the Grand-Duc's table.
quote: The domaine is open for visits on Friday afternoon ... open to the public by appointment ... Domaine Alice Hartmann's Crémants are served at Luxembourg's most prestigious occasions, including parliamentary functions and even at the Grand-Duc's table.

claim: Domaine Cep d'Or in Hettermillen offers tastings and a Tire-Bouchon wine bar/restaurant in a Valentiny-designed building with a panoramic Moselle terrace, with a Vinothèque selling its wines and Crémants.
quote: Visitors can enjoy time with friends or family in the wine bar "Tire-Bouchon" ... one of the most beautiful terraces in the region with an unobstructed view of the Moselle and its vineyards.

claim: Domaines Vinsmoselle, Luxembourg's biggest cooperative producer (since 1921) and home of the Poll-Fabaire Crémant brand in Wormeldange, prices individual tastings from €10, Discovery Tastings €12.50, children's tastings €4.50, age 16+ only.
quote: Individual tastings start at 10€, with Discovery Tastings at 12.50€ and Children Tastings (3-15 years) at 4.50€ ... Wine tastings are only possible for people aged 16 and over.

claim: Musée A Possen, the folklore-wine-and-toy museum in Bech-Kleinmacher housed in seven traditional Moselle houses, is open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00-18:00, €5 adults, children free.
quote: Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 til 18:00. ... Adults: €5 ... Children: Free

claim: The Schengen European Museum, dedicated to the Schengen Agreement at the Luxembourg-France-Germany triangle, is open daily 10:00-18:00 (last entry 17:30), with brief 2026 closures on 9-13 March and an early 3 p.m. close on 27 April.
quote: Open today 10:00 – 18:00 ... March 9-13, 2026: The museum will be closed ... April 27, 2026: The museum will close at 3 p.m.

claim: The Ehnen Wine Museum (Wäinhaus) remains closed for renovation into 2026 with no announced reopening date; when operating, admission was €3.50 adults / €1.50 children with a complimentary wine or juice glass.
quote: The Wine Museum closed its doors for renovation ... Adults: €3.50 (includes wine glass) ... Children under 15: €1.50 (includes juice glass)

claim: The Wormeldange Koeppchen (250m altitude) is one of the most celebrated panoramic viewpoints over the Luxembourg Moselle, with a 1925-1927 chapel to St Donatus and a south-facing shell-limestone Riesling vineyard of national renown.
quote: panoramic view over the village of Wormeldange ... the Moselle valley, and the village of Wincheringen on the other side of the Moselle ... one of the most beautiful and popular viewpoints of the Luxembourgish Moselle ... chapel built in 1925 in honor of Saint Donatus

claim: RentaBike Miselerland offers cheap regional bike rental with free helmet at outlets including Remich Esplanade and Schengen (6 rue Robert Goebbels), and bikes can be returned to any participating outlet on the flat Moselle cycle path.
quote: The regional bicycle hire service RentaBike miselerland is practical, simple and cheap to use ... offers free use of a helmet along with your bike ... Bikes can be returned to any participating outlet.

claim: Driving distance from Moutfort to Echternach is 33 km, about 32 minutes by car.
quote: the driving distance between Moutfort to Echternach is 33 km. It takes approximately 32 min to drive from Moutfort to Echternach.

claim: Driving distance from Moutfort to Beaufort is 37.6 km, about 36 minutes — just outside a 30 km radius.
quote: The road distance is 37.6 km between these two locations in Luxembourg. The journey by car takes approximately 36 minutes

claim: Driving distance from Moutfort to Larochette is 28.3 km, about 32 minutes — inside 30 km.
quote: the driving distance between Moutfort and Larochette is 28.3 km, and the journey takes approximately 32 minutes

claim: Driving distance from Moutfort to Berdorf is 32.9 km, about 33 minutes — just outside 30 km.
quote: the driving distance between Moutfort to Berdorf is 33 km. It takes approximately 33 min to drive from Moutfort to Berdorf.

claim: Beaufort Castle: adult ticket €8, open daily mid-March to mid-November; site combines medieval ruins (1050-1650) and a 17th-century Renaissance residence with guided tour ending in a Cassero blackcurrant liqueur tasting.
quote: Adults: €8.00 ... Daily mid-March to mid-November ... medieval ruins, constructed between 1050-1650 ... 17th-century residence ... tasting of the famous Cassero liqueur (blackcurrant liqueur)

claim: Larochette Castle: €7 adult, open daily 15 March – 15 November 2026, 10:00–18:00 (last entry 17:00); 12th-century medieval ruins on a 50 m sandstone plateau, partly destroyed by fire around 1565.
quote: Sunday, March 15, 2026, to Sunday, November 15, 2026 ... 10:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. ... €7.00 ... medieval ruins positioned on a 50-meter-high sandstone plateau ... fire around 1565

claim: Mullerthal Trail Route 2 is a 39.7 km loop with 387 m elevation gain (~12 h 50 min), starting from Echternach Basilica and passing Schéissendëmpel waterfall, Wollefsschlucht and the Kuelscheier rock fissure.
quote: 39,7 km ... 387 m ... Echternach (Basilica) - Berdorf - Müllerthal - Hersberg - Scheidgen ... Schéissendëmpel waterfall ... Wollefsschlucht ... Kuelscheier

claim: Schiessentümpel waterfall sits on CR121 in Mullerthal village; large parking lot is 500 m from the cascade, with a 1879 sandstone bridge that is the symbol of Luxembourg's Little Switzerland; reachable via Route 3 or local W7 (10.2 km).
quote: CR 121, L-6245 Mullerthal ... between the village of Mullerthal and the crossroads at the Breidweiler bridge ... 500 meters from the waterfall ... sandstone bridge constructed in 1879 is the symbol of the Mullerthal Region

claim: Local trail E1 is a 13.5 km loop (~4 h, 326 m elevation, demanding) from Echternach Basilica through Wolfsschlucht gorge, the Huel Lee cave and the amphitheater millstone quarry.
quote: Length: 13.5 km ... Elevation Gain: 326 m ... Duration: 4 hours ... Wolfsschlucht, described as a steep, smooth rock crevice ... Huel Lee cave and amphitheater

claim: The Predigtstuhl ("pulpit") rock formation outside Berdorf has labyrinth-like passages and stairs carved in the sandstone leading to two viewing platforms, with a small car park at the base on Route 364.
quote: Predigtstuhl is a rocky formation ... pulpit-like shape and narrow passageways carved through the stone, with two viewing platforms ... located along Route 364, and there's a small car park at the base of the rocks

claim: Echternach is Luxembourg's oldest town, anchored by the Abbey founded by St Willibrord in the 7th century and the Romanesque-Gothic Basilica housing his tomb (free entry, donations).
quote: Echternach, with the Abbey of Echternach at its center, is considered the oldest town in Luxembourg. The abbey was founded in the 7th century by St Willibrord

claim: The Wollefsschlucht (Wolf Gorge) near Echternach is a narrow canyon with sandstone walls up to about 50 m high, on Mullerthal Trail Route 2.
quote: spectacular natural canyon with rock walls rising up to 50 meters high

claim: Driving distance from Luxembourg City to Trier is roughly 49 km, about a 46-minute drive — Moutfort sits east of Luxembourg City so trip is similar (~45 km)
quote: The driving distance between Luxembourg and Trier is 30.41 mi (48.93 km), with a driving time of approximately 0h 46min.

claim: Trier's Roman monuments, the Cathedral of St Peter and the Liebfrauenkirche are collectively inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site
quote: Roman Monuments, Cathedral of St Peter and Church of Our Lady in Trier

claim: The Porta Nigra is a 2nd-century Roman fortified gate flanked by two semi-circular four-storey towers and is Trier's signature landmark
quote: The Porta Nigra is an enormous fortified gate built of large stones, flanked by two semi-circular four-storey towers, and is a unique achievement of 2nd century Roman architecture.

claim: The Constantine Basilica (Konstantin-Basilika) in Trier is 32m x 61m and 36m tall, and is the largest surviving Roman building without internal columns
quote: 32m x 61m and 36m tall, doesn't have a single pillar in it, making it the largest building without columns, surviving since Roman Era

claim: Trier Cathedral is the oldest cathedral in Germany, with its core nave built of Roman brick in the early 4th century under Constantine
quote: Trier Cathedral is the oldest cathedral in Germany... central part of the nave was built of Roman brick in the early fourth century

claim: The Liebfrauenkirche, adjacent to Trier Cathedral, is the earliest church built in French High Gothic style outside France (1230–1260)
quote: the earliest church built in French High Gothic style outside France

claim: Karl Marx's birthplace at Brückenstraße 10 in Trier operates as a museum run by the Friedrich-Ebert-Stiftung
quote: Museum Karl-Marx-Haus in Trier

claim: Karl-Marx-Haus summer hours (15 March – 14 November) are daily 10 am–6 pm; winter hours close on Mondays; admission €7 adult
quote: Summer opening hours (March 15 – November 14): Monday – Sunday: 10 am – 6 pm. Winter opening hours (November 15 – March 14): Tuesday – Sunday: 10 am – 6 pm.

claim: The Three-Borders Monument erected in 1997 has three steel columns bearing stars representing the original Schengen signatory countries
quote: Erected in 1997, the monument features three tall steel columns, each bearing a star to represent the first signatory countries of the Schengen Agreement

claim: The Roman Villa Nennig at Römerstraße 11, 66706 Perl, houses a 160 m² mosaic of over 3 million tiles depicting gladiator and animal-hunt scenes, open March–November
quote: one of the most beautiful and largest examples of Roman mosaic art of the 2nd and 3rd century... 160-square-meter floor contains over 3 million tiles

claim: The Nennig mosaic was discovered in 1852 by a farmer and remains in situ, an unusual survival for Roman mosaics north of the Alps
quote: The mosaic at the Roman villa in Nennig

claim: The Upper Mosel cycle path runs from Perl to Nittel along the German Moselle bank through vineyards with no gradients, suited to relaxed wine-village hopping
quote: Mosel Cycle Path Section 1: From Perl to Nittel

claim: Nittel is the standout wine village of the Upper Mosel with numerous wineries, wine taverns and inns clustered in one small town
quote: Wineries | Nittel an der Mosel

claim: The Saarschleife treetop walk and viewpoint near Mettlach is about a 36 km / 42-minute drive from Luxembourg City — outside the strict 30 km radius but reachable in under an hour
quote: the distance between Baumwipfelpfad Saarschleife and Luxembourg is 25 miles (24.2 miles by road). The fastest way to get from Baumwipfelpfad Saarschleife to Luxembourg is to drive, which takes 42 minutes

claim: The Saarschleife is a water gap where the Saar carves a hairpin through quartzite; the Cloef viewpoint sits ~180 m above the river and the Baumwipfelpfad treetop walk opened July 2016
quote: a water gap carved by the Saar River through a quartzite layer

claim: Bourglinster Castle operates as a dining and events venue (two restaurants — La Distillerie and Brasserie Côté Cour — plus salons for weddings/conferences) rather than a ticketed museum, with no public tours advertised.
quote: Available Activities: Dining Options: The castle operates two restaurants... The website makes no mention of public castle tours, museum exhibitions, or general cultural events open to the public.

claim: Bourglinster Castle is ~17 km east of Luxembourg City, was restored after the State acquired it in 1968, and since 1982 hosts exhibitions, concerts and the Friends of Bourglinster Chamber Music Festival.
quote: Bourglinster Castle is located in the village of Bourglinster in central Luxembourg some 17 km (11 mi) to the east of Luxembourg City... After it was acquired by the Luxembourg State in 1968, the buildings were fully restored and, in 1982, opened for exhibitions, concerts, meetings and receptions.

claim: Hollenfels Castle interior is closed for renovation; only the rose garden in front and a path with steep steps to the base of the rock are publicly accessible, and the on-site youth hostel is also temporarily closed for reconstruction.
quote: Due to renovation work, the castle cannot currently be visited from the inside. However, the rose garden in front of the castle is open to the public... The youth hostel Hollenfels is temporarily closed as reconstruction works are underway.

claim: The Valley of the Seven Castles follows the Eisch valley from its confluence with the Alzette upstream to Steinfort; the seven castles are Mersch, Schoenfels, Hollenfels, the old and new Ansembourg, Septfontaines and Koerich, drivable in about an hour or hikeable on a 37-km footpath.
quote: The seven castles are: Mersch, Schoenfels, Hollenfels, the old and new castles of Ansembourg, Septfontaines and Koerich... The entire route can be traversed in about an hour by car... There is also a 37-kilometre footpath.

claim: Useldange Castle ruins host a UNESCO-sponsored discovery trail with 16 tactile and audio stations in English, French, German and Luxembourgish, plus a touchable crypt model and two permanent exhibitions on castle history and medieval daily life.
quote: The castle is unique for its UNESCO-sponsored discovery trail for partially-sighted visitors, weaving around the castle and up into the restored castle tower with a series of 16 tactile and audio experiences.

claim: Pettingen Castle ruin, ~4 km north of Mersch, is a 30-metre-square moated stronghold with four round corner towers, freely accessible 24/7 at no charge; damaged by French cannon in 1684 and state-owned since 1947.
quote: Pettingen Castle is located in the village of Pettingen some 4 km north of Mersch in central Luxembourg. This nice castle ruin is freely accessible, and entrance is free. The castle ruin is open 24/7 so you can visit it anytime you want.

claim: Mersch Castle is a Renaissance structure at Place Saint Michel now used as the commune's town hall, with public access limited to the inner courtyard; the square also features the baroque 1707 tower of the former St-Michel parish church, now a tourist info point.
quote: The building now serves as the town hall and administrative center for the local commune... You can visit the inner courtyard. The square in front of the castle has a 1707 baroque style tower of the former St. Michel church.

claim: Sanem Castle near Esch-sur-Alzette is a 16th-century rebuild (completed 1557, reconstructed around a rectangular courtyard ~1567) that has stood vacant since 2016 after stints as a children's home (Kannerschlass) and refurbishment.
quote: Today's building was completed in 1557 after the medieval castle had been partly destroyed. In about 1567, Frédéric de Hagen-Fleckenstein reconstructed the castle, placing the new buildings around a large rectangular courtyard... As of January 2025, Sanem castle has been vacant since 2016.

claim: Septfontaines Castle (Burg Simmern) in the Eisch valley burned down in 1779 and is privately owned and not visitable inside, but the ruins and rose garden in front are freely accessible year-round.
quote: The castle fell prey to a devastating fire in 1779 and burned down... Today the castle is privately owned and cannot be visited. However, the rose garden in front of the castle is open to the public. Additionally, the castle is freely accessible all year round.

claim: The National Museum of Military History in Diekirch presents WWII and the Battle of the Bulge through ~50 life-size dioramas and tens of thousands of artefacts; open daily 10:00–18:00 May–September and 14:00–18:00 October–April with €6 adult admission.
quote: Using life-size dioramas, the military museum in Diekirch shows realistic scenes from the lives of soldiers in wartime and reconstructs the battles in the surrounding area, with 50 unique dioramas, tens of thousands of exhibits.

claim: Vianden Castle lies ~47 km (about 44–50 min) by road from Luxembourg City, placing it well outside a 30 km radius from Moutfort even after accounting for Moutfort's ~10 km offset south-east of the capital.
quote: Vianden is a 47 kilometres (29 miles) drive from Luxembourg City... the fastest way to drive from Luxembourg to Vianden Castle takes 44 minutes.

claim: Moutfort sits in the Contern commune south-east of Luxembourg City, reachable from the capital in roughly 10–20 minutes by car, which sets the practical centre for a 30 km radius covering the Guttland castles cluster.
quote: Luxembourg City can be reached from Contern in less than 20 minutes... The commune of Contern is reachable by car in 10 minutes from the city of Luxembourg.

claim: Parc Merveilleux Bettembourg 2026 dated tickets cost €15 adult / €11 child (3-14) / free under 3, plus €1.50 per attraction-token ride.
quote: Adults: €15 ... Children (3-14 years): €11 ... Children under 3: Free ... Attraction tokens (mini train, pony express, mini cars): €1.50 per ride or €12 for 10 rides.

claim: Parc Merveilleux is open daily through 11 October 2026, ticket counters 9:30-18:00 and park closes 19:00.
quote: The park is open daily (including Sundays and public holidays) up to and including 11 October 2026. The ticket counters open in the morning at 9:30 AM and close at 6:00 PM, while the park itself closes at 7:00 PM.

claim: Mondorf Domaine Thermal is Luxembourg's only thermal spa, set in a 45-hectare park ~15 km south of Moutfort with a 36°C mineral-rich thermal pool, 11 saunas, and 3 hammams.
quote: MONDORF Domaine Thermal is a true oasis of well-being in Luxembourg, nestled in a 45-hectare park ... The real star is the 36°C thermal pool, with water naturally rich in minerals

claim: Mondorf spa access runs roughly €20-45 depending on duration; the on-site adults-only spa requires guests to be 16+.
quote: prices typically range from €20-30 for adults ... one visitor mentioned paying €45 for 3 hours ... the on-site spa is only accessible for guests aged 16 years or older.

claim: Kockelscheuer ice rink, ~10 km from Moutfort, operates 15 September to 15 April and hosts Disco-on-Ice and Family Afternoons on weekends/holidays.
quote: The ice rink operates from September 15 to April 15. The Skating School offers lessons for children, teenagers, and adults. During holidays and weekends, special events such as "Disco on Ice" and Family Afternoons are held.

claim: The Kockelscheuer site combines the rink with 16 ha of park, ponds and forest, an 8.74 km hiking loop, picnic area, golf, bowling and tennis, with 550 free parking spaces.
quote: 16 hectares of park, ponds, and forest ... an 8.74km hiking route (about 2 hours and 15 minutes of walking) ... 550 places available and is free for 24 hours.

claim: The Three Rivers cycle path PC3 follows the Moselle, Sauer and Our rivers for 89 km from Schengen to Vianden, passing close to Moutfort via Remich.
quote: The Three Rivers Cycle Route follows the course of the Moselle between Schengen and Wasserbillig, the Sauer between Wasserbillig and Reisdorf, and finally the Our between Reisdorf and Vianden. The total length of the route is 89 km

claim: Coque aquatic centre in Kirchberg charges €4.50 adult, €2.30 child and €12.90 family for entry.
quote: The family entry price for the Aquatic Center is €12.90 ... adult entry costs €4.50 and child entry costs €2.30.

claim: Luxembourg's only karting circuit is the ACL-run outdoor track at Mondercange (~20 km from Moutfort); reservation required up to 3 weeks ahead.
quote: Karting Mondercange, the sole outdoor karting facility in Luxembourg, has been thrilling enthusiasts since its establishment in 1974 ... Reservations for individuals are made at the earliest 3 weeks before the desired date.

claim: Mondercange karting sessions cost about €23 for 10 minutes, €42 for 20 minutes, or €58 for 30 minutes per driver.
quote: around 23 euros per person for a thrilling 10-minute ride, 42 euros for an extended 20-minute session, or 58 euros for an adrenaline-pumping half-hour adventure.

claim: 216k Escape Room in Luxembourg City offers themed rooms suitable for children from ~8 years upward, with 1-3 hour games.
quote: both children (from +/- 8 years) and adults will find a game to suit their taste. 216k's escape games guarantee between one and three hours of excitement and fun.

claim: Kikuoka Country Club in Canach (~15 km from Moutfort) welcomes visitors daily with prior booking and requires a valid handicap certificate (max 35 weekdays / 28 weekends).
quote: Visitors are welcome every day, advance booking is essential, and a valid handicap certificate from the player's home club is required. The handicap limit is 35 (Mon-Fri) / 28 (Sat, Sun & Holidays).

claim: Golf Club Grand-Ducal at Senningerberg (founded 1935, ~10 km from Moutfort) has 18 holes plus 6 compact holes and accepts visitor green fees Monday-Friday.
quote: founded in 1935 and is located 7 km from the capital, near Luxembourg-Findel airport. The site has 18 holes and 6 compact holes ... Green-Fees are accepted from Monday to Friday.

claim: Outdoor Freizeit at Dillingen (~35 km north of Moutfort) rents kayaks and canoes on the Sûre from Pentecost through 30 September, departing 10:00-14:00.
quote: Outdoor Freizeit is located at 10, Rue de la Sûre, 6350 Dillingen and offers canoe and kayak departures from Dillingen or Dillingerbrück ... season runs from Pentecost (23–25 May) and 4 June – 30 September

claim: Bambësch forest in Luxembourg City has four waymarked loops (4.6 to 7.5 km) starting from the car park, with restaurants and playgrounds at Sieweburen and Juegdschlass.
quote: four way-marked loops ranging from 4.6km to 7.5km, all starting at the car park ... Juegdschlass and Sieweburen have restaurants with Luxembourgish specialties plus playgrounds.

claim: Aquasud Differdange features 9 pools plus wellness, fitness and beauty zones; adult entry €6, under-16s €5, under-4s free.
quote: an aquatic area with 9 pools, a fitness area with over 20 machines, and a wellness and balneotherapy area ... Adults €6, children under 16 €5, under 4 free.

claim: The Aula Palatina (Konstantin-Basilika) in Trier measures 67 m long, 26.05 m wide and 33 m high, and contains the largest extant hall from classical antiquity, designed with no interior columns.
quote: The hall has a length of 67 m, a width of 26.05 m and a height of 33 m. ... The basilica contains the largest extant hall from classical antiquity ... a lack of columns in the interior and an open, box-like shape.

claim: The official Trier tourism information office describes the Konstantin-Basilika as the largest pillarless hall structure surviving from the ancient world.
quote: the basilica with the largest pillarless hall construction in the ancient world was built for him

claim: The official Visit Luxembourg listing for Caves St Martin in Remich gives a traditional guided tour with tasting at €9.00 per person, lasting one hour, with reservations required 48 hours in advance.
quote: Guided tour with tasting ... 1 hour ... €9.00 per person ... Reservations have to be made 48 hours in advance.

claim: Visit Moselle (the regional Moselle tourism site) corroborates the €9.00 per person, one-hour guided tour with tasting at Caves St Martin Remich, with 48-hour advance reservation.
quote: Guided tour with tasting ... 1h ... €9.00 per person ... Reservations have to be made 48 hours in advance.
